newsitem.title: USA: U.S. teenagers charged in baby death freed on bail.
newsitem.headline: U.S. teenagers charged in baby death freed on bail.

text.p: Two New Jersey teenagers accused of killing their newborn son were freed from a Delaware jail on Tuesday after their parents posted bail of $300,000 each.

Amy Grossberg and Brian Peterson, both 18, were to remain under house arrest temporarily in separate homes in Delaware until an electronic monitoring system was installed in their homes in Bergen County.

Their release came after a Delaware Superior Court hearing in which President Judge Henry DuPont Ridgely set the bail and the conditions under which the teenagers must live at home with their families.
The conditions call for electronic monitoring, an 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew, and a waiver of both domestic and foreign extradition.

Grossberg's parents Alan and Sonye Grossberg thanked supporters after they learned their daughter had been released from prison. The couple held hands throughout a 10-minute interview with reporters arranged by one of their lawyers, Charles Slanina.
"We're just all excited to have her back and to be a family again. We've waited for this for so long ... we just want her home," Sonye Grossberg said.

Slanina said the teenagers were sent to separate private homes in Delaware and would be constantly supervised. "They are in their places of home confinement and reunited with their respective parents," he said, adding the parents were expected to spend the night with their son and daughter.
Slanina said the teenagers would remain in Delaware until the monitoring systems were in place in their homes in New Jersey, which could take anywhere from 24 hours to a week.

Grossberg and Peterson were indicted last month on one charge of intentional murder in the first-degree for which the state said it will seek the death penalty and a second charge of murder in the first-degree by abuse and neglect, for which the state will seek life imprisonment.
According to court records Peterson helped Grossberg deliver a baby boy on Nov. 12 in a motel room in Newark, Delaware, and disposed of the body in a dumpster behind the motel.
According to a preliminary report by the state medical examiner, the infant was alive when born and then fatally injured by being shaken and receiving a blow to the head.

At a court hearing last month, defence attorneys indicated their experts believed the infant would not have survived its own congenital deformities or the medical problems suffered by Grossberg early in her pregnancy.
